question: Can a nonlinear multiview method recover a known coordinate shared across two heterogeneous views while rejecting view-specific nuisance more effectively than concatenated PCA, linear CCA, and concatenated spectral embedding?
hypothesis: On the declared synthetic paired-view fixture, datafold jointly smooth functions recover the known nonlinear common coordinate with low nuisance alignment, outperform the strongest declared baseline, and lose that recovery when cross-view correspondence is shuffled.

datasets.grid: 600 deterministic paired samples generated from the fixture seed
datasets.quality_control_policy: generation is deterministic, finite-valued, shape-checked, and algebraically checks the declared common coordinate

primary_metrics.aggregation_domain: candidate coordinate versus known common coordinate over all 600 paired samples
primary_metrics.missing_data_policy: any non-finite or missing candidate coordinate is experiment failure
primary_metrics.uncertainty_method: deterministic synthetic fixture; no sampling interval claimed

primary_metrics.aggregation_domain: candidate shared-coordinate absolute Spearman minus the maximum of the three declared baseline scores
primary_metrics.missing_data_policy: all candidate and baseline scores are required
primary_metrics.uncertainty_method: deterministic synthetic fixture; no sampling interval claimed

secondary_metrics.aggregation_domain: candidate coordinate versus known observation-specific nuisance over all samples
secondary_metrics.missing_data_policy: candidate and nuisance values are required

secondary_metrics.aggregation_domain: jointly smooth coordinate after deterministic permutation of view-B correspondence versus the original known common coordinate

negative_controls: deterministically shuffle the row correspondence of the nonlinear-observation view while keeping both marginal view distributions unchanged
measure alignment with the declared observation-specific nuisance rather than only measuring recovery of the desired coordinate
compare against a nonlinear spectral method on standardized concatenated views so nonlinearity alone is not credited as multiview structure
falsifiers: jointly smooth functions recover the common coordinate with absolute Spearman below 0.9
the candidate remains aligned with observation-specific nuisance above absolute Spearman 0.2
the candidate fails to exceed the strongest declared baseline by at least 0.15 absolute Spearman
shuffling cross-view correspondence retains common-coordinate absolute Spearman above 0.5
a missing datafold capability silently substitutes another algorithm under the same method identity
split_policy: not applicable to this deterministic synthetic structural fixture; later learned or climate-facing experiments require separate discovery/confirmation splits
preprocessing: each observed view is standardized independently; no target coordinate or nuisance variable is supplied to candidate or baseline fitting
stopping_rule: the reference experiment passes only when all four predeclared candidate, nuisance, baseline-advantage, and shuffled-correspondence guards pass in the pinned environment
multiple_comparison_policy: the four method identities and four guard metrics are fixed by this experiment version; all are reported
